items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: Emmett Hardy, he just, had, had a certain way of playing... Johnny Frisco was on drums, Santo, Emmett Hardy, and, uh, I don't know, Harry Shields or Larry Shields or, or, or Branny. There was, you know, they were supposed to be the jazz clowns

ctx.x: And, and, and it's kind of hard to, to explain. I mean, I, I don't know notes. You understand? Mm-hmm. I mean, I know how to read drum music, but I don't know notes up and down the scale. I studied out there with Earl Hatchett, trying to, trying to learn how to play vibrapholes and stuff like that. But I, I, I could memorize things better and, and, and play it my own way. Mm-hmm. Faster than I could read it. See, I, I'm, I'm slow at reading anything, besides music, you know. So, uh, Emmett Hardy, he just, had,…

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-27
items.q: he, he had a style more, more like Big Spider-Back.

ctx.x: What about Emmett Hardy? What kind of style did he have?
Well, he, he had a style more, more like Big Spider-Back.

items.title: Ray Bauduc Interview, 1984-06-26
items.q: And he had Brownlee playing piano and Emmett Hardy playing cornet and so forth. And then later on, later on I played with Eastwood out at, with Abby Brunson and the guys at the halfway house.

ctx.x: So what was the color of the poise? I don't know whether it was white or black or not. But anyway, I don't remember what color it was until this day. But I answered the wrong one. I said black and it was supposed to be a white horse. And the whole class started to laugh at me. So then I hate to be laughed at. I can't help it. It's human nature that way, everybody. So I said, that's it brother. I said, I'm sorry. I made the mistake. Now let's get down to brass tacks. You take this French book and shove it up your…
